extracted.intended_audience: established biomedical researchers at eligible U.S. institutions considering applying to the HHMI Investigator Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for applicants to the HHMI Investigator Program, including eligibility requirements, the attributes sought in investigators, application materials, and how selection and renewals are assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and pursue significant biological questions
rubrics_metrics.description: They identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attribute is used in review of applicants during competitions and during review of investigators for appointment renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive the field into new areas; be at the forefront
rubrics_metrics.description: They drive their chosen research field into new areas of inquiry, being consistently at its forefront.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI seeks investigators who push the bounds of knowledge and open new directions for inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new tools and methods enabling creative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: They develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions, bringing to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on methodological innovation and interdisciplinary approaches that enable asking previously unapproachable questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forge links between basic biology and medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: They forge links between basic biology and medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators commonly connect fundamental biological discovery to medical relevance or application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of future original and innovative contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: They demonstrate great promise of future original and innovative contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considers not only past accomplishments but potential for continued high-impact work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active in service and training
rubrics_metrics.description: They are active in service and training in their host institutions, and in the greater scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI values mentorship, leadership, and contributions to the scientific community as part of investigator roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD and/or MD required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and/or MD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a baseline eligibility requirement; specific competitions may state additional qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research must be performed at an eligible U.S. institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must plan to perform research at one of over 200 eligible U.S. institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's host institution must be on the list of eligible institutions for the competition (downloads available for eligible institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold a position representing substantial institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a position that represents substantial commitment by their institution, such as a tenure-track faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects applicants to have an institutional appointment that supports sustained research activities; exact acceptable positions may be defined by each competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of peer-reviewed funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a track record of peer-reviewed funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated success securing competitive, peer-reviewed research funding is required evidence of an applicant's research independence and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required length of post-training professional experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines a required length of post-training professional experience prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific minimum number of years post-training is set by each competition and should be checked for the relevant competition announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary breadth defined per competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines the breadth of scientific disciplines to be considered; however, most competitions are open to all biomedical disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should confirm whether a given competition is open to their discipline; most HHMI Investigator competitions accept all biomedical fields but exceptions may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include a CV, five highlighted research articles, and a program description focused on research achievements during the last five years and future research plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program description should emphasize recent accomplishments (last five years) and clearly articulate future research vision and plans; five articles should highlight most significant work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct application; no nomination and no institutional limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants apply directly; there is no nomination process and no limit of the number of applications from a single institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lowers institutional gatekeeping—individual eligible scientists may submit applications without institutional nomination or quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by HHMI leadership and expert panel assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of investigators is made by HHMI scientific leadership and is based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection decisions are informed by external peer assessment and internal leadership judgment; applicants are evaluated against the Investigator Attributes and application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI selects people, not projects
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI supports people, rather than projects, because it’s individual scientists who break barriers to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes the investigator's track record, creativity, and potential rather than a narrowly scoped project plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHMI investigator appointment has a seven-year renewable term. Renewal decisions are made by HHMI scientific leadership, based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal is contingent on continued demonstration of the Investigator Attributes and impactful research; investigators are periodically reviewed for renewal eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment, support, and community expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are employees of HHMI and receive salary and benefits from the Institute. Investigators are provided generous financial support for research as well as access to capital equipment funds. They belong to a community of nearly 300 investigators and attend scientific meetings highlighting Institute science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not evaluative criteria for selection, these program features set expectations for the level of institutional engagement, available resources, and community participation associated with the appointment.
